top_story.headline: South Korea's Korea Foundation Registers Its Washington Office Under FARA
top_story.dek: The Korea Foundation, a statutory body funded by an endowment from Korean passport fees, filed for its D.C. overseas office as Korea Foundation USA.
paragraphs: Korea Foundation USA registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act on October 8 as registrant #7777, with The Korea Foundation of South Korea as its only foreign principal (registrant listing). The registration statement says the registrant is not separately incorporated. It describes itself as the Washington overseas office of the foundation, operating under headquarters' internal regulations, approved plans, personnel arrangements and budgetary control. It lists a D.C. organization date of December 9, 2005, and names Sung Won Bae as director (registration statement).

The Exhibit AB says the foundation was established under the Korea Foundation Act and is categorized by Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy as a Non-Classified Public Institution. It describes its funding as an endowment drawn from Korea's passport issuance fees, managed by the foundation (Exhibit AB). Its stated work is Korean studies, cultural and people-to-people exchange, research and dialogue. The OCR text available here is cut off before the answers on government supervision and financing, and shows no fee or contract terms.

sections.headline: No new ethics filings or divestitures in the window
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics filing system shows no newly submitted divestitures, terminations, or ethics agreements in the past four days. The routine disclosure filings tracked during this window contained no novel restrictions or disclosures requiring separate notice.

sections.headline: One New Registrant, a Madagascar Consulting Extension and a Nigeria Agent Departure
paragraphs: One new registrant, one amended foreign-principal agreement and one individual agent's departure from a foreign-principal engagement were stamped on October 8. No registrants were terminated and no new or dropped foreign principals appeared in the bulk files.

items: New registrant: Korea Foundation USA (#7777), registered 10/08/2026, foreign principal The Korea Foundation (South Korea). Listing; registration statement (a second copy was also stamped: duplicate); Exhibit AB.

Sonoran Policy Group, LLC D/B/A Stryk Global Diplomacy (#6399) filed an updated Exhibit AB for Harena Resources PLC (United Kingdom), now named Harena Rare Earths PLC. Under the extension, signed 9/9/2026, the International Consulting Agreement dated May 5, 2026 runs from August 6 through November 5, 2026. The client pays US$50,000 plus expenses, and services performed since August 6 are treated as covered. The consultant advises the client on engagement with U.S. government officials regarding the Republic of Madagascar. The agreement ends November 5 unless the parties sign a further extension. Exhibit AB; amendment.

DCI Group AZ, LLC (#6278) filed an amendment reporting that Nick Lewis ended his relationship with the foreign principal Republic of Nigeria through Aster Legal on 08/01/2026 because he ceased working on the project. The filing was stamped 10/08/2026, 68 days after that date. Amendment.

sections.headline: One Filing: A Texas Senate Candidate Report
paragraphs: No House filings and no stock-trade reports appeared in this window. The only new disclosure is a Senate candidate report from a Texas candidate.

items: Jade Simmons (Senate candidate, Texas; candidacy commenced 08/17/2026), candidate report filed 10/08/2026. She reports $250,000 in self-employment income from Jade Media Global, LLC of Kingwood, Texas, and no reportable assets, honoraria, gifts, travel, positions or agreements. Liabilities: an educational loan of $50,001-$100,000 owed to the U.S. Department of Education, deferred during the campaign, and two revolving charge accounts at Chase Bank of $10,001-$15,000 and $15,001-$50,000. Filing.

sections.headline: No New Registrations; Ten Terminations and a Wave of Third-Quarter Reports

There were no new registrations. The table lists all ten terminations and the activity reports with the clearest signal: former officials, large spending and live fights. Most of the 298 activity reports are not detailed.
